issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'מֹטוֹת עֻלָּם' means 'the bars of their yoke' (construct chain: מֹטוֹת = bars/staves of, עֻלָּם = their yoke). The Chinese renders it as '他們軛的軛' ('the yoke of their yoke'), which is a duplication error — the word '軛' (yoke) appears twice, but the Hebrew has two distinct nouns: 'מֹטוֹת' (bars/staves) and 'עֻלָּם' (their yoke). This changes the meaning, as the Hebrew refers to breaking the bars of the yoke, not a doubled 'yoke of yoke'.
